people.name: Aaditeshwar Seth
people.bio: Aaditeshwar Seth is a professor in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering at the Indian Institute of Technology Delhi, and co-founder of the social technology enterprise Gram Vaani and of the CoRE stack infrastructure and network. He is passionate about building appropriate technologies and participatory tools that can empower marginalized communities to collectivize and voice themselves, and especially to build climate resilience. Several million people, and over 200 organizations worldwide, have directly touched technology platforms built by Aaditeshwar’s team at Gram Vaani, the CoRE stack, and his students at the ACT4D (Appropriate Computing Technologies for Development) research group at IIT Delhi. Many elements of their work have also been adopted by government departments and have influenced the use of technologies for development in the social sector. He is a recipient of the ACM SIGCHI Social Impact Award for 2022. His book published in 2022, Technology and (Dis)Empowerment: A Call to Technologists, argues that the primary goal of technologists should be to bring equality and overturn unjust social and economic structures through their inventions.
people.designation: Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering

people.name: Abhas Abhinav
people.bio: Abhas is a hacker, entrepreneur and free software activist. He is the founder of DeepRoot GNU/Linux, an twenty-six-year-old Free Software Business that provides support, services and solutions for Free Software deployments. DeepRoot builds mail servers and clusters, provides hosting & support for a variety of Free Software tools and helps organisations of all sizes choose self-hosting for their infrastructure in general. Abhas also leads a hardware venture called Mostly Harmless, where he experiments with and builds Libre and Liberated Hardware (like hackable mechanical keyboards, liberated computers, home automation solutions, cameras, lights and more). The goal is to build and sell hardware put owners in control of their lives by enabling them to run free/libre software on more hardware than usually possible. Mostly Harmless operates the LibreTech.Shop - India’s first store for hackable and ethical products that offer convenience. Abhas is a member of the the Free Software Foundation, India working group and has been a participant in the community in India for many years.

I have published work in the same, besides having founded HackerFab IITB last year at my university - building open-source semiconductor fabrication equipment. LLMs have made it possible even for software noobs like me to fiddle around with building small tools and apps - I have made a few in the past, and this is a more ambitious attempt at the same.

people.name: Aman Dalmia
people.bio: I love building tools that help propagate the benefits of technology to people it wouldn't reach by default and have spent the last 8+ years applying AI to solve problems in agriculture, healthcare and education. After graduating from IIT Guwahati, I was a part of the founding team of Wadhwani AI where we built AI systems to advise cotton farmers on the optimal time to spray pesticides (winner of the Google AI Impact Challenge in 2018), identify low-birth weight babies and screen for COVID-19 using cough sounds.  At Avanti Fellows , we built open-source learning tools (winner of the Tools Competition in 2023) to enable effective and engaging online learning for government school students.  At Noora Health , I led the development of an AI copilot for nurses to reduce their turnaround time in responding to queries regarding maternal and child health for millions of caregivers across Bangladesh, Indonesia, India and Nepal. Most recently, I have been building Calibrate , an open-source AI agent evaluation platform for non-profits and Formbharo , a form-filling voice agent for public health, at Artpark . At Agency Fund , I work closely with their grantees to strengthen their AI evals and conduct workshops on the best practices for evaluating AI systems in development. I love open-source. Some of my other significant open-source projects are: SensAI , an open-source AI-powered LMS to help educators automate assessments and an AI coach that provides real-time, personalized support to every learner, used by HyperVerge Academy for training youth from low-income backgrounds to get jobs in tech. Plio , an open-source tool that converts any YouTube video into an interactive lesson. It helped Avanti Fellows increase the completion rate on their lesson videos by 5 times for 40k+ government school students during the pandemic and is currently being used by other non-profits for improving engagement on their video lessons. Some of my past work has also been published at top conferences such as KDD, ICLR, and CVPR. For more details, please check: https://amandalmia.com/

people.name: Bodhish Thomas
people.bio: Bodhish Thomas is the CEO of the Open Healthcare Network Foundation, engineer, founder, open-source leader, and speaker. He is the creator and architect of Open Healthcare Network, a Digital Public Good that powers critical healthcare infrastructure across multiple Indian states. Founded during the pandemic, OHC has grown from an emergency response initiative into a community-driven healthcare technology ecosystem stewarded by the Open Healthcare Network Foundation. His open-source portfolio includes CARE, MediSpeak, MyTemplate, and AfterFlood, alongside significant contributions to Pupilfirst LMS and the broader Digital Public Goods ecosystem. Bodhish has been at the forefront of using technology and AI to solve complex challenges in healthcare, education, and public infrastructure, building systems that are designed not just to scale, but to serve. Recognized as one of the first recipients of GitHub’s Open Source Grants from India and now a GitHub Star, Bodhish has demonstrated a rare ability to build technology, mobilize communities, and sustain impact at scale. He also serves as a board member of FOSS United, contributing to the growth of India’s free and open-source software movement. With a vision for systemic change, Bodhish continues to show how open source, community stewardship, and digital public infrastructure can become powerful catalysts for societal transformation.

His work on Indian Kanoon — which has made millions of court judgments freely searchable — directly informs the design philosophy behind Repub.

people.name: Durwasa Chakraborty
people.bio: I am a PhD scholar in the Department of CS at IIT Madras, advised by Dr. KC Sivaramakrishnan and Dr. Kartik Nagar. My research focuses on programming languages and the formal verification of concurrent systems, that is, formally proving that concurrent programs are correct. I completed my undergraduate studies at Government Engineering College, Jabalpur, and my master's at Northeastern University, Boston. Before returning to academia as a full-time PhD student, I spent some years in industry as a software engineer at IBM, MathWorks, and AWS, building distributed systems, cloud infrastructure, and data pipelines, which gave me the financial stability I then heroically abandoned for intellectual freedom and a tax-free stipend. Outside research, I faithfully perform the sacred duties of every software engineer: watching anime, playing guitar, and carrying a camera everywhere in the hope of one day accidentally taking a good photograph. I occasionally write about algorithms, computer science, academia, and assorted obsessions under "Anachronistic Monk," at durwasa-chakraborty.github.io.

people.name: Mishi Choudhary

She is currently the SVP and General Counsel at Virtru, a global data encryption and digital privacy provider. Under her direction, SFLC.in became the premier non-profit organization representing the rights of Internet users and free software developers in India. In 2015 she was named one of the Asia Society’s 21 young leaders building Asia’s future. In 2016 she was inducted into the Aspen Global Leadership Network by the Aspen Institute. She advises Columbia University’s Global Freedom of Expression project and serves on the Board of IFEX and Global Network Initiative.

people.name: Saalim Quadri
people.bio: I'm Mohammad Saalim, a Software Engineer at 63SATS and a community-driven open-source developer who somehow turned flashing custom ROMs and compiling Android as a teenager into a full-time career. My journey into Android started more than six years ago with a simple curiosity: how does Android actually work beneath the UI? What began with custom ROMs, kernels, and device bring-up quickly grew into a deep interest in Android platform development. Since then, I've spent countless hours working across Android Frameworks, Launcher3, Chromium, Linux kernels, BSPs, and embedded Linux systems. Professionally, I've worked on Android bring-up efforts, Android Framework development, Launcher3 maintenance, Chromium fork, Raspberry Pi Android ports, Linux kernel development, and embedded Linux distributions built using Yocto and Buildroot. I'm also a Google Summer of Code contributor with The Linux Foundation, where I worked on integrating ROS SDK into Automotive Grade Linux through the meta-ros yocto layer. Outside of work, I lead Team Stormbreaker, an open-source community focused on Android and Linux Kernel development. I enjoy reverse engineering Android components, exploring platform internals, mentoring newcomers entering the Android ecosystem, and sharing the lessons I've learned along the way. If it runs Android or Linux, there's a good chance I've tried compiling, porting, modifying, or breaking it at least once.
